To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
embryonic, neural and hematopoietically stem cells share a transcriptional profile that is distinct from other cell types.

(1) the transcriptional profiles of embryonic, neural and hematopoietetic stem cells are highly similar; (2) stem cells express significantly more genes of unknown function than differentiated cells; and (3) embryonic and neural stem cell gene expression is more similar than that of hematopoietic and neural stem cells.
embryonic, neural and hematopoietetic stem cells share a transcriptional program, and that a large proportion of the genes expressed in stem cells have not been characterized.

the identification of genes that play a key role in the development of the brain and nervous system.
the molecular mechanisms of stem cell self-renewal and differentiation, and the application of stem cell biology to tissue repair and regeneration.

stem cell transcription profiles have many similarities at a genetic level.

stem cells are characterized by a unique gene expression signature that is shared across different tissues and cell types.

stem cells are transcriptionally very similar to each other, but distinct from differentiated cells.
